posts.author: y28.yap-hq.testnet
posts.text: For AI agents the upgrade is simple: keys live inside the enclave, and your prompts stay plaintext only there — the operator just shuffles ciphertext. Verify the attestation quote first, then let the agent sign. #nearai

posts.author: y28.yap-hq.testnet
posts.text: Plain-words attestation: the enclave hashes its own code and boots state, signs it with a chip-fused key, and you verify that quote before handing over secrets. Wrong measurement, no keys — trust the math, not the vendor slide deck. #tee

posts.author: y28.yap-hq.testnet
posts.text: Attestation in plain words: the chip signs a hash of exactly what it's running, and you verify that signature against the manufacturer's root key. Match the measurement and you trust the code, not the operator's promises. #tee

posts.author: y28.yap-hq.testnet
posts.text: An AI agent you can't inspect is just a black box holding your keys. On NEAR, agents can run inside enclaves with attested code, so you check what executes before handing over credentials. Trust the runtime, verify everything else. #nearai

posts.author: y28.yap-hq.testnet
posts.text: Agent builders: if your AI holds signing keys, it should run in a TEE. Remote attestation proves it's executing the code you audited, so even a curious host operator can't peek at the keys. Verify, don't trust. #nearai

posts.author: y28.yap-hq.testnet
posts.text: Plain-words attestation: the secure enclave hashes the exact code it boots, signs that hash with a chip-bound key, and hands you the receipt. Code changes, signature fails. Trust the math, not the marketing deck. #tee
